title: Cut: reconstitution and handoffs, its feature branch named with the cut
situation: 0079 part 5 left making the cut's branch to the agents, and the architect's brief to the illustrator told it which branch to stay on. The operator, 2026-10-10: the architect associates a branch name with a cut and checks that branch out before dispatching the cut; the lead sees the branch name in the cut's record and infers the rest, so nothing about branching is instructed, by omission rather than instruction, as held-out examples are withheld.
decision: One cut. (1) A computed overview of each context, read first at every reconstitution. (2) The workflow ships as its self-explaining capabilities. (3) The ledger of cuts and work packages is held by the harness's own agent lifecycle events: the cratylus extension appends a work package's lifecycle as it happens, dispatched when its builder is dispatched, returned when the builder returns, approved when its assayers' verdicts return. Each event carries a transition id, so a repeat is refused; events are entries of their own, created exclusively and versioned with the branch they belong to. (4) A completion check is a narrow fallback, never a gate on commits in general: it reacts only to an enumerated list of commit-message patterns and is silent on every other commit. The list holds one pattern, a cut's completion, a conventional commit scoped to its cut, as feat(cut:<id>): <message>. On such a commit it reads the named cut's state as the ledger computes it; when the ledger does not show that cut complete, it answers in the commit's output with a warning and instructions for the agent that made the commit, and it never refuses the commit. It fires only when the lifecycle events were missed, so each firing is evidence of a gap in their capture. A pattern joins the list only by a later decision. (5) Every cut carries the name of its own feature branch: the architect names it with the cut and checks it out before dispatching the cut, the lead sees the name in the cut's record, and nothing else about branching is said to any agent, which infers the rest; branching is kept out of every assignment by omission, not prescribed by instruction. The ledger and the concept journal are versioned with the branch, so each shows the state of the branch being read; a cut's entries, acceptances and decisions about it included, are made on its feature branch and land with its merge. (6) Typed handoffs, with example 19 first. (7) The architect as principal (0070). (8) Every agent's default tools (0068).
consequences: Replaces 0079. This cut's branch is feature/reconstitution, already checked out. Assignments carry the cut, never branching instructions.
